data.one_liner: A floating panel window that can be dragged, spring-snapped, parked, and expanded.
data.what_it_does: Provides a draggable floating panel widget for Flutter that snaps to screen edges using physics-based motion. It supports collapsing to a small window or parking off-screen as a grab tab, and expands in place on tap.
use_when: You want a floating picture-in-picture style player or utility window.
You need a panel that can be tucked away to the screen edge when not in use.
avoid_when: You need standard modal bottom sheets or navigation routes.
Your content requires complex layout constraints within a small bounding box rather than full-window overlay.
strengths: High-performance rendering with custom RenderBox painting that avoids rebuilding app subtrees during motion.
Physics-based spring motion derived from native SwiftUI fluid interfaces.
weaknesses: Must be mounted globally over the full window (e.g., via MaterialApp.builder) to position correctly.
Expanded builder runs even while collapsed, so expensive subtree setup must be avoided or gated.
data.minimal_example:
MaterialApp(
  builder: (context, child) => DraggablePanel(
    collapsedBuilder: (context, status) => const Icon(Icons.play_arrow),
    expandedBuilder: (context, status) => const MiniPlayer(),
    child: child,
  ),
  home: const HomeScreen(),
)
